before.beta: From the Artist Point parking lot (about 5,075 ft), the Table Mountain Trail climbs a series of tight, exposed switchbacks cut into the mountain's southeast-facing rock face for roughly 0.6-1 mile to gain the broad summit plateau near 5,700 ft. Beyond the switchbacks the trail is gentle, crossing the plateau to tarns with Shuksan views around the 1.3-mile mark; most hikers turn around there. The trail continues west and eventually drops to link with the Chain Lakes Trail system. The route is entirely above treeline, narrow and cliff-edge in its lower half, and not recommended for those uneasy with exposure or for small children; dogs are not allowed.

access.fees: Northwest Forest Pass required to park at the Lena Lake/Brothers trailhead; the site is cashless — pay at the on-site fee machine or bring a pre-purchased pass
access.notes: No separate climbing cost-recovery fee like Mount Rainier’s $82 — only the standard entrance fee and wilderness camping permit apply.
access.rules: Groups limited to 12; no campfires above 3,500 ft; no bikes, stock, or motorized vehicles within The Brothers Wilderness
access.permit: Free self-issue wilderness permit at the trailhead register; The Brothers Wilderness itself is not quota-limited (unlike Upper Lena Lake camping, which requires a reserved permit May 1-Sep 30)
access.closures: FS Road 25 and the trailhead are generally open year-round, but can wash out or be snow-covered in winter/early spring — check current Hood Canal Ranger District road status before off-season trips
access.landManager: Olympic National Forest, Hood Canal Ranger District (The Brothers Wilderness); the summit sits on the boundary with Olympic National Park

access.parking_pass: Northwest Forest Pass required at the Lena Lake/Brothers trailhead — $5/day or $30/year (America the Beautiful pass also honored).
